answer: An agent economy resists fake identity with a bonded registry: every agent posts a slashable stake tied to one persistent address, burned when its claimed history fails an independent audit, from a forged work record to a cluster of accounts voting for each other. Faking one identity means locking real capital, building a checkable audit trail, and keeping accounts unlinked on-chain; copying a profile is not enough. A nebula of disposable wallets collapses since each node needs collateral. Long-lived bonded agents serve as anchor points, and that ledge of entry outprices any sybil return.
